newsitem.title: INDIA: India SAIL, other steel firms seen hurt by budget.
newsitem.headline: India SAIL, other steel firms seen hurt by budget.

text.p: The state-run Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) will be adversely affected by a reduction in import duty on cold rolled steel announced in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget on Friday, analysts said.
"Overall, it is negative for SAIL," Anuradha Rao, analyst at Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL), said.
SAIL is India's largest dealer in cold-rolled steel, selling over one million tonnes annually. SAIL officials were not immediately available for comment.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, presenting his 1997/98 budget to parliament, said he proposed to lower the import duty on cold-rolled steel to 25 percent from 30 percent to help India's engineering industry.
"We'll be revising earning estimates for SAIL," said a steel analyst at a European brokerage who declined to be identified.
"It's a blow for the cold-rolled steel industry which is already in trouble," V.S. Bapna, director of Ispat Industries, told Reuters after the finance minister released his proposals.

He said if the proposal led to increased import of cold-rolled steel, it could adversely affect domestic producers of hot-rolled (HR) steel too. HR steel is the raw material for the manufacture of cold-rolled steel.
"Stand-alone CR players such as NSL will be hurt as they don't do much of value addition," CRISIL's Rao said.
Other CR producers appeared to be well protected, she said.
She said automobile manufacturers stood to benefit from lower CR prices.
A series of recent cost increases -- in power, coal and rail freight -- would also hit steel firms, analysts said.
